title: context-footprint-burst-scheduler-estimate-2026
content:
Purpose:
Estimate cross-region GPU buffer needs and context/cache pressure for a new compact model that has high multi-tenant locality and a larger per-session context footprint. This sheet is an engineering-first sketch to: 1) quantify steady-state vs burst buffer GPU needs; 2) surface eviction risk windows for the context cache; 3) propose a minimal seeding schedule for the burst scheduler.

High-level summary (one-paragraph):
Model: compact-v2 (quantized 4-bit), typical serving variant has 8k context support but average active context used per session is ~3.2k tokens. Primary risk: increased key-value (context) working set per concurrent session increases memory pressure on per-GPU KV cache and reduces headroom for batching. With conservative arrival spikes (1.6x baseline sustained over 12 minutes) regions with <10% free GPU headroom will face increased tail latencies. Recommendation: provision a small per-region burst buffer (2-4 GPUs) and enable aggressive prefix sharing for identical-session detection during the first 30s of a session.

Assumptions and inputs (source rows):
- baseline qps per region (observed week-of-Feb): us-west-2: 480 qps, eu-west-1: 210 qps, ap-southeast-1: 70 qps
- avg requests per session: 4.2 (user turns that create/extend context)
- avg new tokens per request: 64 tokens
- average active context window per session (tokens): 3200 tokens
- per-token stored KV size (post-quantization metadata + pointer): 6 bytes/token (incl. compressed attention keys + small header)
- overhead per context root (session record): 1.5 KB
- GPU model and memory: A100 80GB usable per node for model + KV cache (assume 68GB available to KV after model residency and batching memory)
- KV eviction policy: LRU with 10% reserved non-evictable working set for pinned prefixes
- expected burst multiplier (short spikes): 1.6x baseline for 12 minutes, once per day per region during new model rollout traffic patterns

Derived numbers (calculation rows):
- per-session KV bytes = (3200 tokens * 6 bytes) + 1500 bytes = 19200 + 1500 = 20700 bytes ~ 20.2 KB/session
- average concurrent sessions baseline per region = baseline qps * avg session length (we assume 30s active window) * 1 / requests-per-session => simplify: concurrent_sessions ~= qps * 30 / 4.2
  - us-west-2: 480 * 30 / 4.2 = 3429 concurrent sessions (baseline)
  - eu-west-1: 210 * 30 / 4.2 = 1500 concurrent sessions
  - ap-southeast-1: 70 * 30 / 4.2 = 500 concurrent sessions
- baseline KV working set per region = concurrent_sessions * 20.2 KB
  - us-west-2: 3429 * 20.2 KB = ~69.3 GB
  - eu-west-1: 1500 * 20.2 KB = ~30.3 GB
  - ap-southeast-1: 500 * 20.2 KB = ~9.9 GB
- available KV capacity per GPU node: 68 GB
- GPUs required for baseline KV if dedicated to KV (conservative separable calc) = ceil(baseline working set / 68GB):
  - us-west-2: ceil(69.3/68) = 2 GPUs (just over 1)
  - eu-west-1: ceil(30.3/68) = 1 GPU
  - ap-southeast-1: ceil(9.9/68) = 1 GPU

Burst analysis (1.6x sustained for 12m):
- concurrent_sessions_burst = concurrent_sessions * 1.6
  - us-west-2: 5486 sessions -> KV working set ~110.8 GB
  - eu-west-1: 2400 sessions -> ~48.5 GB
  - ap-southeast-1: 800 sessions -> ~16.2 GB
- GPUs required during burst (KV footprint only):
  - us-west-2: ceil(110.8/68) = 2 GPUs (still 2 but now very tight; eviction pressure high and tail latency risk)
  - eu-west-1: ceil(48.5/68) = 1 GPU
  - ap-southeast-1: ceil(16.2/68) = 1 GPU
- note: these GPU counts assume a single GPU can be used for both model execution and KV. In practice contiguous model residency and batch memory will reduce KV usable to ~50–60GB depending on concurrency, which increases required GPUs. Use conservative factor of 0.8 -> effective KV per GPU = 54 GB -> recompute recommended buffers below.

Effective KV capacity (conservative): 54 GB per GPU
- us-west-2 baseline GPU need = ceil(69.3/54) = 2
- us-west-2 burst GPU need = ceil(110.8/54) = 3
- eu-west-1 baseline = ceil(30.3/54) = 1
- eu-west-1 burst = ceil(48.5/54) = 1
- ap-southeast-1 baseline = ceil(9.9/54) = 1
- ap-southeast-1 burst = ceil(16.2/54) = 1

Buffer recommendation (per-region):
- us-west-2: add 1 dedicated buffer GPU (makes baseline fleet for this model 3 GPUs assigned to KV/model residency to absorb 1.6x spikes)
- eu-west-1: no immediate buffer required but reserve preemption policy to borrow 1 GPU from dedicated inference pool if burst persists > 10 minutes
- ap-southeast-1: no buffer required, monitor for traffic growth and KV pressure (threshold: 12GB free KV capacity)

Eviction pressure & latency risk windows:
- With conservative KV=54GB/GPU and LRU policy, us-west-2 will experience meaningful eviction when >~2 concurrent sessions churn per second with unique prefixes that are not shared. Eviction causes additional recompute when evicted KV is requested, increasing per-token cost and tail latency.
- Risk period: first 30–90 minutes after traffic shift during rollout due to new user patterns (less prefix sharing).

Burst scheduler seeding plan (operational rows):
- Goal: pre-warm the context cache for top-10 heavy prefixes observed in beta traffic and maintain a 30s sliding window prefix-seed for identical sessions.
- Seed window: run prefix seeding every 5 minutes in us-west-2 for the first 72 hours of rollout; reduce to 15 minutes after stable metrics for 48 hours.
- Seeding volume: target top-1000 prefixes, each with synthetic traversal of up to 5 tokens to ensure KV entries are materialized without fully replicating user tokens (privacy-safe hash mapping).
- Scheduler throttle: cap seeding QPS to 2% of baseline region QPS to avoid adding noise to production load metrics.

Operational runbook (short checklist):
- Before rollout: ensure capacity reservations for +1 GPU in us-west-2; configure autoscale to allow preemption borrowing in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.
- During first 24 hours: monitor 95/99th p50 token latency, KV eviction rate (events/min), and free KV capacity per GPU.
- If eviction rate > 0.5 events/sec for >10 minutes, trigger emergency scale: add 1 GPU to region and increase seeding frequency to 1m for top-500 prefixes.

Simplicity checks and caveats:
- This sheet assumes a single per-session working set size. Real sessions vary; heavy tail could double per-session KV (e.g., multi-turn assistants). Add multiplicative risk factor for assistant workloads (+1.8x per-session KV).
- Quantization of KV entries may improve effective per-token bytes; we used 6 bytes/token as a conservative estimate. If we validate 4 bytes/token in profiling, buffer needs drop ~33%.
- Cross-region routing: If latency-based routing funnels users to us-west-2, we must revisit buffer sizing — this calc is per-region independent.

Decision needed (short):
- Approve +1 dedicated buffer GPU in us-west-2 for rollout week? (ops sign-off required)
- Approve seeding plan above (privacy-safe hashed pseudo-seeding) to be run during first 72h?

Next steps and owners:
- Action: run microbenchmark to measure per-token KV bytes (Alyssa) — target: measure empirically across 3 workloads by 2026-03-09.
- Action: ops to create a short-lived reserved GPU for us-west-2 (Marcus) — target: provision by 2026-03-06.
- Action: implement seeding scheduler prototype in infra-runner (Riley + Sanjay) and gate behind feature flag — target: feature branch by 2026-03-10.

Notes and links to follow-up analytics queries:
- Suggested PromQL for KV eviction rate: sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (region)
